title: "Lifting for looks is feminine"
summary: NH dismantles the claim that lifting for looks is feminine or vain, arguing it is swole-shaming born of envy. He traces it to 'power coppers', lifters who wanted aesthetics, failed, and now claim to only care about strength while idolizing aesthetic strongmen and doing curls. He argues intent is required to avoid an accidental physique and urges bodybuilders to own their goal.
claims: Calling lifting for looks feminine is always meant to shame and really means vain or gay; it says more about the speaker than the target
By that logic anyone who showers or dresses well is feminine
Accusations of vanity or narcissism from non-lifters are attempts to make you stop doing something that makes them uncomfortable as your confidence grows
Even if lifting were vain, a society of vain people beats one of self-haters; confident people tend to be strong and strong people tend to be virtuous
Hard-earned body development breeds pride and confidence, traits essential and attractive in men
Building muscle is the best way for a man to look better, beyond clothes and grooming
Lifters tend to be anti-consumerist, independent and anti-authority, traits linked to success
Makeup is feminine because it mimics female fertility markers; muscle likewise signals male fitness and good genes to women, so it is masculine
Big quads were once called feminine, but male quads look nothing like female quads and masculine archetypes always had big legs
Scrutinizing other men's bodies to call them feminine is jealousy and passive aggression
Greek statues, gods and heroes were muscular without performing any function; muscle itself expresses masculinity
The cartoon superheroes of his childhood were all big and strong, giving his generation male power fantasies
A power copper wanted an aesthetic physique, failed, and now claims he never wanted it, like a child refusing the toy he could not get
Saying natural bodybuilding is a joke is a near-certain sign of a power copper
The final stage of the cope is claiming the best way to get big is to get strong
The 'thick' dad-bod look is reframed as aesthetic by those who did not lift for looks; Greek statues had no gut for a reason
Real strength athletes do not deride lifting for looks; he has good relations with natural powerlifters and mutual respect
Power coppers only idolize lifters who are both big and aesthetic, such as Eric Bugenhagen, whose comment section is mostly about his physique
Power coppers who claim not to care about looks flex in their thumbnails and profile pictures
Claiming curls are for bench carryover is a lie; any carryover is negligible and curls are done for looks
Training purely for strength produces an accidental physique: big trunk and quads, small arms, which most find unappealing
Training with aesthetic intent is essential to avoid an accidental physique
Bodybuilders have accidental strength: weaker than powerlifters but much stronger than average
A psychiatrist told him poor mental health is marked by failing to align the physical and the spiritual
Hemingway, whom he covered in about 20 episodes, is the archetypal power copper whose life derailed
A 260 lb lifter mocking a 200 lb lifter for being weaker shows he does not understand weight classes
Being 260 lb and benching 350 lb would not place at a natural meet
If what you want is aesthetics, say you are a bodybuilder; inventing a function backstory only hurts yourself
exercises: done for looks; bench carryover is a myth
